# Scientific formatting validation: H<sub>2</sub>O

## Abstract

This is synthetic layout evidence, not a scientific report. The source explicitly distinguishes the *OsD18* gene from the OsD18 protein and preserves the botanical name *Arabidopsis thaliana*. An *in silico* example supplies typography only [1].

## Mixed scientific notation: Fe<sup>3+</sup>

Ordinary area m<sup>2</sup>, water H<sub>2</sub>O, and a literal raised reference-shaped token <sup>[2]</sup> remain source typography. Only this outside reference [2] navigates to the bibliography. **Strong text**, *italic text*, and ***combined text*** retain their faces.

### Linked labels and combinations

The authored [H<sub>2</sub>O label](https://example.org/molecules) remains one ordinary link. A composed *italic x<sup>2</sup>* and **bold y<sub>i</sub>** preserve both styles. Adjacent x<sup>2</sup><sub>i</sub> remains two independent spans.

- List notation: H<sub>2</sub>O alongside the *OsD18* gene.
- A second list item retains its explicit citation [1].

> A quoted Fe<sup>3+</sup> example must keep its raised charge inside the line box.

## Table containment

| Specimen | Source-authored notation | Deliberately long explanation | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| *Arabidopsis thaliana* | H<sub>2</sub>O; Fe<sup>3+</sup> | This synthetic cell is deliberately long so that the current writer must wrap words within the column without overlapping the neighboring cell or table borders. | [1] |
| *OsD18* gene / OsD18 protein | **x<sup>2</sup>** and *y<sub>i</sub>* | Adjacent styles must not split a word unnecessarily; the mixed upper and lower runs must contribute to the measured row height. | [2] |
| Synthetic long identifier | ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 | Long tokens remain complete and use the existing measured break policy. | Literal <sup>[2]</sup> |

Figure 1. Synthetic H<sub>2</sub>O and Fe<sup>3+</sup> caption text; no image is fetched by this fixture.

## Literal and rejected input

Encoded <sup>2</sup> and inline code `<sub>2</sub>` stay literal. A mismatched <sup>2</sub> is visible and does not consume this outside citation [1]. Nested scripts <sup><sub>2</sub></sup> remain literal.

Entity-decoded line breaks stay within one source-authored script: x<sub>i
jk
l</sub>. This case tests text preservation, not a scientific formula.
